title: Lathoa 让 AI 故意算错，孩子找出错误才能得分
summary: Lathoa 把 AI 的不可靠性变成教学资产，通过让孩子找出机器人 Errol 解题步骤中的故意错误来练习批判性思维，但难点在于稳定制造恰到好处的错误。
opening: Lathoa 是一个面向 10 到 14 岁孩子的数学应用，它的核心玩法是让一个叫 Errol 的机器人分步解数学题，其中某一步故意出错。孩子需要找出错误步骤并解释原因，有时题目没有错误，孩子必须判断“没有错误”才能得分。这个产品最让我感兴趣的地方，不是它用了 AI，而是它把 AI 的不可靠性变成了教学资产。但真正难的地方在于，如何稳定地制造“恰到好处的错误”。
core_experience:
在 Lathoa 的首页上，你可以不注册直接玩一个案例。我看到的流程是：Errol 展示一道数学题的分步解答，其中一步被标记为可疑。孩子需要判断哪一步错了，并用自然语言解释错误原因。如果孩子认为没有错误，也可以选择“没有错误”。系统会根据判断的准确性和解释的质量给予 XP，速度越快得分越高。整个过程中没有与 LLM 的直接对话，所有交互都通过结构化界面完成。

产品背后的验证机制值得拆解。每个案例在呈现给孩子之前都会经过检查：先用确定性算术检查重新计算，再用第二个模型独立求解，如果两者与 Errol 的答案不一致，案例就会被丢弃。这种设计确保了故意错误是真实且可解释的，避免了“AI 假装错误但实际正确”的尴尬。错误分为三个难度等级（Obvious、Sneaky、Expert），匹配不同年龄和技能水平。
why_it_works: Lathoa 有效的原因在于它把学习目标从“得到正确答案”转向“识别错误推理”。认知科学中的错误检测学习和自我解释效应表明，分析错误解决方案比单纯学习正确方案更能促进深层理解。产品通过强制孩子解释错误原因，激活了元认知过程。同时，验证闭环解决了 AI 生成内容不可靠的问题：算术检查和第二模型交叉验证确保了每个呈现给孩子的错误都是真实且可解释的。游戏化设计（如 Errol 的表情变化、侦探等级）提供了即时情感反馈，降低了学习过程中的挫败感。
boundaries: Lathoa 的验证机制有一个明显的弱点：第二模型可能与第一模型犯同样的错误，导致验证失效。算术检查只能覆盖部分问题类型，对于更复杂的数学推理或非算术类问题，验证的可靠性会下降。此外，速度奖励可能鼓励孩子快速猜测而非深入思考，与培养批判性思维的目标存在潜在冲突。目前产品仅覆盖数学领域，且错误类型可能过于基础，难以满足高年级或能力较强的学生。验证步骤的具体实现细节未公开，难以评估其鲁棒性和对复杂问题的覆盖能力。
personal_judgment: Lathoa 代表了一种有趣的产品方向：不试图让 AI 变得完美，而是利用其不完美来创造学习机会。这种“反向利用”的思路在 AI 产品设计中很有启发性。然而，产品的长期价值取决于它能否持续生成高质量、多样化的错误案例，并有效管理验证成本。如果验证环节过于依赖人工或计算资源，规模化将面临挑战。此外，产品需要证明其学习效果优于传统练习，而不仅仅是新颖有趣。我认为，Lathoa 的真正创新不在于 AI 技术本身，而在于将 AI 的不可靠性转化为可控的教学工具，并通过产品设计（如无聊天界面、结构化案例）来规避风险。

transferable_methods.name: 故意引入可验证的错误
transferable_methods.principle: 在 AI 生成内容中故意植入错误，但通过独立的验证机制确保错误是真实且可解释的，从而将 AI 的不可靠性转化为教学或测试资源。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于教育、培训、质量评估等场景，需要用户识别错误或异常，且错误本身可以被客观验证。

transferable_methods.name: 用验证闭环约束生成内容
transferable_methods.principle: 在生成内容后增加独立的验证步骤（如确定性计算、第二模型交叉检查），只有通过验证的内容才呈现给用户，以降低 AI 幻觉或错误的风险。
transferable_methods.applies_when: 适用于对内容准确性要求高的场景，如教育、医疗、法律等，且验证成本可接受。

product_takeaway: AI 产品经理可以从 Lathoa 学到：不要试图让 AI 变得完美，而是设计机制来利用或约束其不完美。通过验证闭环和结构化交互，可以将 AI 的不可靠性转化为可控的产品特性。

Things parents actually ask.
Everything parents want to know before getting started.
What age is Lathoa for?
Built for kids 10–14. The case difficulty adapts: younger kids get one-step number checks, older kids get multi-step word problems where Errol's mistake is buried three lines down. It works equally well at the homework table or on a tablet in the back seat.
How is this different from a tutor or Khan Academy?
Tutors and Khan teach kids to get the right answer. Lathoa teaches kids to spot a wrong one: the skill they'll need every time they ask an AI for help. They're complementary, not competing.
Is this safe for my kid? What about AI safety?
Errol is powered by AI, but every problem goes through a separate verification step before your kid sees it. If the AI tries to claim 2+2=5, verification catches it; if Errol's 'wrong answer' isn't actually wrong, we discard it and try again. So you get the variety of generated content with the safety of verified math. There's no open-ended chat. Kids interact with structured cases; they don't talk to a model.
What subjects are covered?
Math today: arithmetic, fractions, ratios, pre-algebra, early geometry, all aligned to Common Core 4–8. Reading comprehension and basic logic are next on the roadmap, with science to follow.
Can I cancel anytime?
Yes. Cancel anytime from the billing portal, no phone call or email gauntlet. The 7-day trial every new account gets needs no card, so there is nothing to cancel when it ends. Monthly plans cancel at the end of the cycle and you keep access until then.
Does my kid need their own device?
No. Lathoa runs in any browser, on iOS, and on Android. The Family plan supports up to 4 profiles on one account, so siblings can share an iPad and the app remembers who's who from a 4-digit PIN.

sources.title: About Us | Lathoa
sources.excerpt:
Every AI tutor races to be correct. Lathoa is the opposite: a critical-thinking gym where kids practice catching AI's mistakes. The one skill no AI can fake for them.
In a world drowning in AI-generated content, critical thinking is the skill that matters most: knowing when an answer doesn't add up, when to push back, when to verify. Lathoa builds this skill in kids ages 10–14 the only honest way: by having them catch a real AI making real, verifiable mistakes. We start with math because math is the only subject where wrong is provably wrong: a deterministic solver checks every problem so Errol's mistakes are never accidentally correct. Reading comprehension and basic logic launch in summer 2026.
Why "Deliberately Wrong"?
Research in cognitive science shows that error-detection is one of the most effective ways to learn. When students actively search for mistakes, they engage more deeply with the material than when passively receiving correct answers. Lathoa turns this insight into a game: kids become "Error Detectives" who help a well-meaning robot learn from his mistakes.
The Science Behind Lathoa
Our approach is grounded in research on productive failure, error-detection learning, and self-explanation. Studies show that students who analyze incorrect solutions develop stronger conceptual understanding than those who only study correct ones. By asking kids to explain WHY something is wrong, Lathoa builds the kind of deep understanding that transfers to new problems.
Lathoa was founded by educators and engineers who believe that the best way to learn isn't to memorize answers: it's to question everything. We're building the tools that help the next generation think critically in an AI-powered world.
